question: Who is the author of the famous novel "The Guide"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**R.K. Narayan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **R.K. Narayan** is the celebrated author of the novel **"The Guide"**, which was first published in **1958**.
 
• The novel is set in the fictional town of **Malgudi** in **South India**, a recurring setting for many of his literary works.
 
• The story follows the journey of the protagonist, **Raju**, who transforms from a professional tour guide to a corrupt manager and eventually to a revered **spiritual guide** or **saint**.
 
• For this masterpiece, **R.K. Narayan** was honored with the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1960**, marking the first time the award was given to an **English-language** work.
 
• The novel achieved further popularity through its **1965** film adaptation, also titled **"Guide"**, starring legendary actors **Dev Anand** and **Waheeda Rehman**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Salman Rushdie**: He is a world-renowned **British-Indian** novelist known for his works in **magic realism**. His famous works include **"Midnight's Children"**, which won the **Booker Prize** in **1981**, and **"The Satanic Verses"**.
 
• **Ruskin Bond**: An **Indian** author of **British** descent, he is famous for his stories set in the **Himalayan foothills** of **Mussoorie**. His first novel was **"The Room on the Roof"**, written at the **age** of **17**. He received the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1992** for **"Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra"**.
 
• **Amitav Ghosh**: He is a prominent **Indian** writer known for his historical fiction, such as **"The Shadow Lines"** and the **"Ibis Trilogy"**. In **2018**, he became the first **English-language** writer to receive the **Jnanpith Award**, India's highest literary honor.
 
• **Malgudi Days**: This is a famous collection of short stories by **R.K. Narayan** published in **1943**, which was later adapted into a popular **television series** in the **1980s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **R.K. Narayan** (**Rasipuram Krishnaswami Iyer Narayanaswami**) was born in **1906** in **Madras** (now **Chennai**) and is considered one of the three leading figures of early **Indian English literature**, alongside **Mulk Raj Anand** and **Raja Rao**.
 
• He was nominated to the **Rajya Sabha**, the upper house of the **Indian Parliament**, in **1986** for his contribution to **literature**.
 
• During his long career, he received several high civilian honors, including the **Padma Bhushan** in **1964** and the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2000**.
 
• His debut novel, **"Swami and Friends"** (**1935**), introduced the world to the town of **Malgudi** and its charming characters.
 
• The themes of his writing often revolved around the **social life**, **middle-class struggles**, and **traditions** of **India**, delivered with a unique blend of **humor** and **compassion**.
</ul
